text: Writing clean code is a skill that makes life easier for you and your team. The main goal is readability—code that is easy to understand at first glance. Good naming conventions are essential. Use clear, descriptive names for variables and functions, like `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `ctp`. This way, anyone reading the code knows its purpose without needing extra comments. Break your logic into small, single-purpose functions. Each function should do one thing well, which makes testing and debugging simpler. Ultimately, clean code boosts maintainability. When you or another developer revisit the project months later, you can quickly make changes without breaking anything. It saves time, reduces frustration, and leads to higher-quality software.
